summary: Documentation, schemas and tests only: docs/protocol.md (+ German twin) and docs/protocol/*.json specify the existing router-agent tunnel protocol as version 1 (ADR-0107, proposed); test/protocol_schema.py (dependency-free validator), test/selftest_protocol.py (added to ci.yml) and agent/protocol_conformance_test.go bind the specification to the router, the Go agent and test/fake_agent.py. No router or agent code, configuration, version, dependency or wire change. Traced B3: login (challenge, Ed25519 signature over nonce|node|pubkey, 32-KiB hello, enrollment limits, revocation), frame dispatch, request streams and the agent passthrough allowlist were read in registry.py, tunnel.py, poll.py, agent/tunnel.go, passthrough.go, heartbeat.go, facts.go; the documentation matches the code and the new tests now cross-check the allowlist (TM-14), the hello and its refusal cases (TM-07) and the update order fields (TM-13) in CI. B8: update and Ollama update orders are only described, their verification is unchanged. B9: one added CI step with no new action, permission or dependency; AGENTS.md gains a documentation rule and weakens no review policy. Tests bind only loopback (aiohttp TestServer, httptest) and start the fake agent as a subprocess without credentials. The published details (limits, message fields) were already public in the open code; the docs add that the configuration bundle (MQTT password) and the update token are secrets agents must not log. Examples use reserved domains/ranges only.

tests.evidence: Ran 20 tests OK on Windows (Python 3.12) and under WSL Ubuntu Python 3.11 in the local CI run; includes rejected cases (hello without pubkey/sig/t, 65-character node name, facts not an object -> 401; OLLAMA without up or with non-list tags dropped; POWER with unknown state dropped).
ok on Windows; TestProtocol* include a refused nonce shorter than 16 bytes and signature verification of the real hello.

tests.evidence: gofmt empty, vet clean for host, windows and linux.

tests.evidence: Undocumented fake-agent heartbeat field, router read/sent undocumented fields, undocumented Facts field, renamed/retyped heartbeat property, extra control-message property, changed allowlist and extra required hello field each made the tests fail; all reverted.

tests.command: python test/selftest_agent_revocation.py; python test/selftest_power.py; python test/selftest_english_names.py; python test/check_pinned_references.py

tests.evidence: index regenerated with ADR-0107; see limitations for the numbering gap.
No Go toolchain in the local WSL; GOOS=linux go vet passed, CI runs go test on Linux and Windows.

limitations: python test/check_adr_index.py reports a numbering gap (0101-0106 are assigned to parallel pull requests not yet on main); it turns green once those merge, as planned by the maintainer's merge order.

The local WSL CI run showed failures unrelated to this change and its files: git ls-files in a Windows worktree (pinned references), missing python packaging and pwsh, and the PostgreSQL integrations; this PR touches no session, memory or storage code.
Pre-existing, not changed here: a heartbeat the router cannot apply is answered with the exception text in HBACK error to the approved agent; the router fails an open stream on an unknown frame type.

The specification describes what the code does today; it does not prove the absence of protocol flaws. Values and patterns are checked by the Python validator; the Go side checks structure, types and required fields.
